newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe's feeds trade pins hopes on dollar's dip.
newsitem.headline: Europe's feeds trade pins hopes on dollar's dip.

text.p: Europe's cash meals and feeds trade remains locked in a volatile U.S. weather market but sellers are hoping the dollar's dip from recent peaks may drag the buyers back in this week.

Chicago's weaker new crop trend, following rainfall reports in the key growing areas of the Midwest, was expected to cause Europe's compounders to hold off purchases in the near term, but analysts reckon they should look to extend winter cover soon.

"If compounders don't change their buying strategy soon, they will risk later on paying a premium over the winter months. My advice is to buy the dips on November to April," said Arie van Dijk of stasticians Stigevo.
But generally, high compounder coverage and adequate immediate arrivals would keep a lid on nearby activity, he said.
Also the possibility of a bumper U.S. soybean this season had increased the likelihood of weaker prices later in the year and was helping to sideline buyers on more distant positions.

But traders said concerns over a potential gap in soymeal supplies in northwest Europe -- caused by South American beans running dry and the first arrivals from the new U.S. crop in September/October -- had sparked activity in European hipro.
Van Dijk highlighted Europe's poultry sector as one which had to take on additional cover soon.

A similar situation was also affecting sunmeal, where old crop material from Argentina was runnning low, leaving a gap which would not be filled until the European harvest appeared on the market in October.
With little unsold material on the water, prices for available sunmeal jumped sky-high to $140 a tonne traded last week, against quotes for July shipment at $123.
Cattlefeed ingredients looked to be ample from now until September, and prices for cornglutenfeed and citruspulp could be pressured as a result.
"There is no room for additional coverage," Van Dijk said.
